themes.name: Sustainability Competencies and Literacy
themes.definition: This theme involves the development and assessment of specific skills, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to sustainability in educational contexts, as observed in various interventions focusing on action competence, systems-thinking, and literacy.
evidence: [ÁlvEmp_2024] SL boosts the impact of academic courses regarding action competences in students
[MuhFos_2024] sustainable competences indicated that HEI and stakeholder respondents identified disciplinary competences as the most important competence cluster
[RukPro_2024] Intrapersonal competence was rated as their highest sustainability competence

themes.name: ESD Pedagogical Approaches
themes.definition: This theme encompasses the various teaching methods and strategies used to facilitate Education for Sustainable Development, including experiential learning, problem-based learning, online learning, and transformative pedagogies, as described in multiple abstracts.
evidence: [YosEff_2022] online learning method in the Moodle forum environment
[MamEmp_2026] experiential learning theory, place-based education, and transformative learning

themes.name: Institutional Integration of ESD
themes.definition: This theme focuses on the processes and strategies for embedding sustainability into higher education institutions, including policy development, organizational change, and institutional frameworks, as evidenced by case studies and frameworks.
evidence: [LevOrg_2021] process of creating and implementing sustainability competencies across a university
[RajThe_2024] context and concept of higher education for sustainable development (HESD) in Nepalese higher educational institutions (HEIs)
[ZúñEdu_2022] knowing the views that prevail in the teaching staff becomes relevant to ensure an effective organizational change of the university curriculum

themes.name: Measurement of ESD Impact
themes.definition: This theme involves the use of assessment tools and methods to evaluate the effectiveness of ESD initiatives, including surveys, tests, and evaluation frameworks, as highlighted in studies measuring outcomes.
evidence: [ChiEva_2025] Pre- and post-course assessments were conducted

themes.name: Student-Centered Learning in ESD
themes.definition: This theme emphasizes creating learning environments that support student engagement, empowerment, and development of sustainability-related skills and attitudes, with a focus on safe spaces and innovation.
evidence: [SinFac_2022] safe enough spaces to navigate these situations of uncertainty
[BraStu_2021] students’ innovation develops in interdisciplinary student teams

themes.name: Faculty and Educator Roles in ESD
themes.definition: This theme addresses the transformation and development of educators in integrating sustainability into teaching, including faculty training, professional growth, and reflective practices.
evidence: [AhmFro_2025] embedding sustainability into university courses acts as a catalyst for educator transformation
[DeCInt_2024] faculty learning community (FLC) to assess how well it prepares faculty
[ZúñEdu_2022] views that prevail in Mexican university professors regarding education for sustainable development

data.meta_observations: The abstracts consistently frame ESD within higher education, with a strong focus on competency development, diverse pedagogical methods, and institutional integration. There is a notable emphasis on assessment and student outcomes, with less attention on faculty roles in some contexts.
data.grounding_notes: Evidence is limited to explicit statements in abstracts; some abstracts have quality issues such as missing elements, which may affect the comprehensiveness of themes. All article keys are from the provided closed set, and no quotes were fabricated or paraphrased.
